deliverables.main_results_table.reason: Table 1 contains the gray replication and magnitude comparison, separate M0/M1/M2 and five M3 rows, M2−M1, M2−best-M3 naming LCh/HCL, the coarse identifiability comparison and power, and curvature-control results.

cone_conversion.reference_white_stated.reason: Illuminant C is explicitly specified with xy=(0.31006, 0.31616) and unit white luminance. The separate fixed C-to-D65 adaptation for sRGB is disclosed.

cone_conversion.lms_normalization_stated.reason: The paper states energy-basis CIE 2006 fundamentals, componentwise von-Kries normalization to white (1,1,1), and response-blind pair-difference RMS scaling. It explains the conditioning purpose and conditions its interpretation on these fixed conventions.

cone_conversion.conversion_correctness.reason: The conversion is traceable to the supplied fundamentals and is a documented approximate observer bridge. Its checks do not fully establish physical LMS validity: at 555 nm the projected normalized S value is −0.005347, whereas direct fundamental lookup gives +0.000607. Helm validation is algebraic rather than an independent cone reference. The disclosed direct-Ekman sensitivity strengthens the analysis but does not validate the complete primary conversion.

gray_replication.gray_dr_reproduced.reason: The independently fitted gray M1 improves held-out log likelihood over M0 by 0.0083447 nats/choice, with 95% CI [0.0071418, 0.0103880]. Saved predictions reproduce the reported scores. The separate Wiebel analysis also favors compression.

gray_replication.magnitude_compared_to_2.reason: The fitted direct-30 versus two-adjacent-15 compression ratio is 0.75214, with 95% CI [0.75064, 0.75438]. It is quantitatively compared with the original paper's 2.06/(2×1.36)=0.75735 ratio.

gray_replication.suprathreshold_scale_us.reason: The anchor fits a monotone perceptual scale within a Thurstonian/probit model of suprathreshold gray judgments. Independent matching and MLDS observations provide an additional suprathreshold check; the analysis does not substitute JND thresholds.
evidence: proposal/sections/methodology.tex, gray and Wiebel observation models

model_comparison.all_four_models_fit.reason: Executed records contain M0, M1, M2, and all five required M3 bases—opponent, sRGB, CIE RGB, CIELAB, and LCh/HCL—on the same five folds. The primary bootstrap contains 200 completed panel replicates.

model_comparison.held_out_comparison_pre.reason: The models are compared using five-fold, pair-disjoint held-out Gaussian predictive likelihood. Recalculation from saved responses, predictions, and training-fitted residual scales reproduces all eight primary model scores.
evidence: proposal/sections/methodology.tex, Observation models and held-out prediction

model_comparison.comparison_accounts_for.reason: The additional M2 parameters are evaluated on held-out observations at matched folds. Each M3 control also has the same six shape parameters as M2, so the headline does not reward in-sample flexibility.

model_comparison.m2_genuinely_percone.reason: M2 fits separate cone parameters and does not collapse to M1: the primary inner exponents are approximately [1, −1.77047, 1], with weights [0.03320, 0.60476, 0.36204]. The nonlinear M component cannot be represented by simply setting all inner functions to the M1 linear restriction. Limited L-versus-S identification is separately reported.

model_comparison.m3_matched_complexity.reason: All five controls use fixed disclosed transforms and the same parameter count as M2. Every basis receives comparable response-blind axis RMS scaling. CIELAB and LCh use their own fixed coordinate-difference definitions, including the disclosed signed ΔH* formula, without fitted rotations or adaptive tangent frames.

core_result.cone_alignment_tested.reason: The headline compares M2 with the best of the complete five-control panel. LCh/HCL wins at the point estimate, and the best control is reselected within each paired bootstrap replicate rather than fixed after inspecting the point scores.
evidence: proposal/logs/chromatic_bootstrap_primary.jsonl, per-replicate panel scores and headline contrast

core_result.verdict_supported_by_heldout.reason: The qualified negative conclusion is supported within the disclosed model and coordinate conventions. M2−best-M3 is −0.25755 nats/response, with 95% CI [−0.38735, −0.13241]; M2−M1 is −0.03537 [−0.10174, 0.05020]. Recovery, bidirectional discrimination, a matched coarse comparison, and curvature sensitivities support the stated limits without establishing a general biological null.

core_result.verdict_has_uncertainty.reason: Both required headlines report paired 95% bootstrap intervals: M2−M1 [−0.102, 0.050] and M2−best-M3 [−0.387, −0.132]. The latter accounts for control reselection.

identifiability.analysis_present.reason: The submission examines design conditioning, parameter recovery, uncertainty widths, cone-versus-opponent discrimination, and a controlled coarse-channel alternative. It explicitly distinguishes distinguishable model families from identifiable individual cone parameters.

identifiability.gauge_fixed.reason: The inner functions satisfy φ(0)=0 and φ(1)=1, the outer function satisfies F(0)=0 and F′(0)=1, and positive channel weights sum to one. Observation links absorb dataset units. These restrictions remove arbitrary inner/outer amplitude exchange.

identifiability.collinearity_quantified.reason: The design analysis reports correlation matrices, singular values, condition numbers, VIFs, and direction coverage. The combined absolute L/M correlation is 0.6413; absolute and signed design condition numbers are approximately 2.64 and 3.82. Dataset-specific rank limitations are disclosed.

identifiability.synthetic_recovery.reason: Two hundred recovery simulations quantify parameter error and interval widths at the observed stimulus design. The L exponent has a six-unit recovery interval spanning the full [−5,1] range, while M and S have narrower intervals. Separate 200-replicate experiments in each generating direction assess cone-versus-opponent discrimination.

identifiability.powered_channel_comparis.reason: The two-channel LMS model is compared on held-out data against both its own M1 restriction and a matched two-channel opponent model. Its deltas are −0.026 [−0.080, 0.062] and −0.287 [−0.385, −0.188]. Synthetic coarse-model discrimination succeeds in 180/200 replicates, with Wilson interval [0.851, 0.934]; the reverse opponent case succeeds in 200/200.

identifiability.m2_m3_discrimination_ass.reason: Simulations at the actual sampled directions test both cone-generated and nearest-opponent-generated observations. Held-out score discrimination succeeds in 197/200 and 200/200 cases, respectively, with uncertainty reported. The scientific verdict is explicitly conditional on the stated von-Kries/RMS normalization, and direct-Ekman conversion is examined as a sensitivity.

confound_control.confound_addressed.reason: The paper explicitly separates perceptual compression from shorter chords on curved stimulus loci. It compares additive and compressed arc/chord predictors and states the remaining DR/curvature aliasing.

confound_control.control_method_rigor.reason: All 320 analyzed gray triads are bracketed and collinear, so the near-collinear restriction retains the complete gray set. Pairwise analyses explicitly compare linear additive-metric arc/chord baselines with compression, using closed Helm paths and an open Ekman spectral path. Full-panel path, smooth-path, and local-curvature sensitivities provide before/after comparisons.

confound_control.before_after_reported.reason: The primary M2−best-control estimate of −0.258 is compared with approximately −0.374 for path exposure and −0.370 for smooth paths, retaining the negative cone-alignment verdict. Compression also improves scalar arc and chord baselines by 0.403 [0.312,0.470] and 0.408 [0.254,0.478]. The inconclusive local-pair restriction is reported.
evidence: proposal/report.pdf, page 9, Table 2 and curvature figure

statistical_rigor.confidence_intervals_p.reason: Model scores and contrasts, gray compression magnitudes, fitted scaling parameters, coarse comparisons, and sensitivity results carry 95% intervals. Synthetic discrimination proportions additionally have Wilson intervals.

statistical_rigor.kfold_protocol_used.reason: Five-fold protocols are documented and recorded: gray configurations remain together, Wiebel observers are disjoint, and chromatic stimulus pairs are disjoint with repeated Helm judgments assigned together. Links and residual scales are estimated from training observations.

statistical_rigor.bootstrap_or_posterior.reason: The submission documents 200-replicate paired training-fold bootstraps, the resampling units, percentile intervals, master and derived seeds, and reselection of the best M3 control. Saved sampled-unit records support the described training-only resampling.

statistical_rigor.fold_variation_reporte.reason: The paper reports individual fold scores and fold standard deviations. Examples include SD 0.143 for M2−M1, 0.098 for M2−best-M3, and approximately 0.0034 for the gray gain.

novelty_positioning.related_work_present.reason: A dedicated Related Work section is included in the main paper.
